==English== {{wp}} ===Alternative forms=== * {{alt|en|draught||British spelling|_|of some senses}} ===Etymology=== {{root|en|ine-pro|*dʰregʰ-}} A phonetic spelling of {{m|en|draught}} (compare {{m|en|laughter}}), from {{inh|en|enm|draught}}, {{m|enm|draght|t=that which is pulled; that which is drawn up, a design}}, from {{inh|en|ang|*dreaht}}, {{m|ang|*dræht}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*drahti}}, {{m|gmw-pro|*drahtu}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*drahtuz|t=a pulling, drawing}}. Cognate with {{cog|nl|dracht}}, {{cog|de|Tracht}}, {{cog|is|dráttur}}. {{surf|+suf|en|draw|t|id2=th}}. ===Pronunciation=== * {{IPA|en|/dɹɑːft/|a=RP,Southern England}} *: {{rhymes|en|ɑːft|s=1}} * {{IPA|en|/dɹæft/|a=US}} * {{IPA|en|/dɹaft/|a=Northern England}} * {{IPA|en|/dɾaft/|a=Scotland}} *: {{rhymes|en|æft|s=1}} *: {{audio|en|En-us-draught.ogg|a=US}} *: {{audio|en|EN-AU ck1 draught.ogg|a=AU}} ===Noun=== {{wikidata lexeme|L9585}} {{en-noun|~}} # {{lb|en|US spelling}} {{n-g|Senses relating to a current or flow or an amount which flows:}} ## A [[current]] of [[air]], usually coming into a [[room]] or [[vehicle]]. ## The [[draw]] through a [[flue]] of [[gas]]ses or [[smoke]] [[result]]ing from a [[combustion]] [[process]]. ## An act of [[drinking]]. ## The [[quantity]] of [[liquid]] (such as [[water]], [[alcohol]], or [[medicine]]) [[drink|drunk]] in one [[swallow]]. ##: {{syn|en|swig|Thesaurus:drink}} ##: {{ux|en|to drink at a '''draft'''}} ##: {{ux|en|She took a deep '''draft''' from the bottle of water.}} ## A [[dose]] (of [[medicine]], [[alcohol]], etc.). ## {{senseid|en|beer}}{{cap|liquid}}, especially [[beer]] or other [[alcohol]], [[draw]]n from a [[cask]] or [[keg]] rather than a [[bottle]] or [[can]]. ##* {{quote-book|en|year=1863|author=Thomas George Shaw|title=Wine, the Vine, and the Cellar|page=152 |text=From 1767 to 1774 no pale wine was bottled but for immediate use; only '''draft''' wine of all kinds was used in the principal taverns, and it was often very bad, not from tricks of the vintners, but from bad management.}} ##* {{quote-book|en|date=2015-09-14|author=Jeff Smith|title=Craft Cider: How to Turn Apples into Alcohol|publisher=The Countryman Press|isbn=9781581575859 |text=Another positive trend is the increase of quality in '''draft''' cider options. '''Draft''' cider has often been, and sometimes still is, considered an inferior product by cider traditionalists, who believe a true cider should come in a bottle or{{nb...}}}} ## {{senseid|en|Q244777}} {{lb|en|nautical}} The [[depth]] of [[water]] [[need]]ed to [[float]] a particular [[ship]]; the [[depth]] from the [[waterline]] to the [[bottom]] of a [[vessel]]'s [[hull]]; the depth of water [[draw]]n by a vessel. # {{lb|en|in both|_|US spelling|and|UK spelling}} {{n-g|(Preliminary) written work:}} ## A [[version]] of a [[written]] [[work]] (such as a [[book]] or [[paper]]) or [[drawing]]. ##: {{ux|en|I have to revise the first '''draft''' of my term paper.}} ##: {{ux|en|His first '''drafts''' were better than most authors' final products.}} ## An [[unsent]] [[e-mail]]. ## A [[preliminary]] [[sketch]] or [[outline]] for a [[plan]]. ## {{senseid|en|order for payment}} {{lb|en|archaic}} An [[order]] for [[money]] to be [[pay|paid]]; the [[document]] that states it: a [[cheque]], [[note#English:_document promising payment|note]], [[bond#English:_Q11693|bond]], [[bill of exchange]], [[money order]]{{,}} or [[IOU#Noun|IOU]]. # {{lb|en|in both|_|US spelling|and|UK spelling}} {{n-g|Senses relating to conscription or selection from a pool:}} ## {{lb|en|American English|Canadian English|usually with '''the'''}} {{cap|conscription}}; the system of [[force|forcing]] people to [[serve]] in the [[military]]. ##: {{ux|en|He left the country to avoid the '''draft'''.}} ## A person who has been drafted; a [[conscript]] or [[draftee]]. ##* {{quote-book|en|year=1889|year_published=1899|author={{w|Rudyard Kipling}}|title={{w|Under the Deodars}}|chapter=Only A Subaltern|location=Boston|publisher=The Greenock Press|page=135|text=With these counsels, and many others equally valuable, did Papa Wick fortify Bobby ere that last awful night at Portsmouth when the Officers' Quarters held more inmates than were provided for by the Regulations, and the liberty-men of the ships fell foul of the '''drafts''' for India, and the battle raged from the Dockyard Gates even to the slums of Longport, while the drabs of Fratton came down and scratched the faces of the Queen's Officers.}} ## {{lb|en|politics|American English}} A system of [[force|forcing]] or [[convince|convincing]] people to take an [[elected]] [[position]]. ## {{lb|en|sports|American English}} A system of [[assign]]ing [[rookie]] [[player]]s to [[professional]] [[sports]] [[team]]s. ## {{lb|en|gaming}} A style of play in collectible card games, where players select from a shared pool of cards. ## {{lb|en|British English|possibly|archaic}} A [[quantity]] that is [[requisition]]ed or [[draw out|drawn out]] from a [[larger]] [[population]]. ##* {{quote-book|en|year=1982 |title=Letters of John Maxwell, Superintendent of Government Stock|author=John Maxwell; Brian Edmund Lloyd; Bertha Mac Smith |page=206 |ISBN=|passage=The Complaint about the Beef lately furnished for the use of the Troops &c at Parramatta, is not without foundation; when I commenced supplying the several Stations with animal food in January last, — a '''Draft''' of very fat Oxen was brought from Wellington for that purpose, — that '''draft''' has met the consumption of several Stations until now. — the Cattle lately remaining fell very much off in condition, though I certainly consider they were not inferior to a great deal of Beef, I have seen taken from Contractors.}} ##* {{quote-book|en|year=2009 |title=A Cavalryman in the Crimea|author=Philip Warner |page= |ISBN=|passage=The Light Brigade have got a '''draft''' of about 250 horses from England, and we expect ours shortly.}} # {{lb|en|US spelling}} The [[bevel]] [[give|given]] to the [[pattern]] for a [[casting]], so that it can be [[draw]]n from the [[sand]] without [[damage|damaging]] the [[mould]]. # {{lb|en|US spelling}} {{n-g|Senses relating to pulling:}} ## {{lb|en|rail}} The [[pull]]ing [[force]] ([[tension]]) on [[coupler]]s and [[draft gear]] during a [[slack]] ([[stretch]]ed) [[condition]]. ## {{lb|en|possibly|archaic}} The action or an act (especially of a [[beast of burden]] or [[vehicle]]) of [[pull]]ing something [[along]] or [[back]]. ##: {{ux|en|using oxen for '''draft'''}} ##: {{ux|en|shot forth an arrow with a mighty '''draft'''}} ## {{lb|en|possibly|archaic}} The act of [[draw in|drawing in]] a [[net]] for [[fish]]. ## {{lb|en|possibly|archaic}} That which is [[draw in|drawn in]]; a [[catch]]; a [[haul]]. ##: {{ux|en|He cast his net, which brought him a very great '''draft'''.}} # {{lb|en|Appalachia}} {{n-g|A valley, or the stream that flows through it:}} ## A [[small]] [[stream]] or [[tributary]]. ##* {{quote-book|en|year=2003|author=John Alexander Williams|title=Appalachia: A History|page=113 |passage=Hollows were tributary to a cove or another type of sizable valley threaded by a creek or, in Pennsylvania, a “run,” and in Virginia, a “'''draft'''.”}} ##* {{see more citations|en}} ## {{lb|en|especially|Virginia|West Virginia|Pennsylvania}} A [[ravine]] or [[narrow]] [[valley]], especially one through which a [[stream]] (at least [[intermittently]]) [[flows]]. ##* {{quote-book|en|year=1887|author=Andrew Smith McCreath; Edward Vincent D'Invilliers|title=The New River-Cripple Creek Mineral Region of Virginia |passage=[page 24:] About one quarter of a mile up the '''draft''', the same blue-gray limestone is opened in a quarry on the Graham and Robinson farm, {{...}}
[page 31:] Up along a narrow '''draft''' heading south-east from the creek at Southern's place, a series of small pits and trenches have been dug close to the ridge {{...}} above the level of the creek.}} ##* {{quote-journal|en|year=1894|author=Charles D Lanier|title=Sawney's Deer-Lick|journal=Scribner's Magazine|page=101 |passage=Then came the pleasant toil up and down the ridges and '''drafts''' of the Knob.}} ##* {{quote-journal|en|year=1894|author=Charles D. Lanier|title=On the Trail of the Wild Turkey|journal=Harper's New Monthly Magazine|volume=89|issue=534|page=883 |passage=Now you have left the dividing "backbone", and climb up and down a never-ending succession of ridges and "'''drafts'''," as the ravines are called. {{...}} a searching reconnoitre of the next long '''draft''' opened to view.}} ====Usage notes==== Although ''draft'' is usually an American spelling, some senses are universal, being used in both British and American English.
